title: P0 host hang: terminal-callback runtime-reset dispatch deadlocks on the runtime's own sessions mutex while global state is held (waiters grew 88→102)
outcome: P0 host hang: terminal-callback runtime-reset dispatch deadlocks on the runtime's own sessions mutex while global state is held (waiters grew 88→102)
acceptance: A deterministic owned-child regression drives an actual terminal Codex callback, in both the normal and the deferred-completion path, into a queued dispatch with runtime_reset_required, through the shared-session detach and re-attach. It completes with no re-entry on the runtime sessions map, delivers exactly one Prompt to a successor with the correct profile, and leaves sibling sessions and global state live. The success, failure and non-reset controls are kept.

When a newer turn of the same runtime is inserted between the extraction and the application of a deferred terminal action, the stale action refuses every lifecycle, capacity, delivery and cleanup effect, and the replacement mapping survives.
The shared-Codex test suites and the full gate pass on the exact pair-reviewed input.

completion.summary:
The P0 host deadlock is fixed. Shared Codex terminal callbacks now extract a SharedCodexTerminalEffect under the runtime sessions guard and apply it only after the guard is dropped. Each effect carries its owner: runtime token, generation and Arc attachment identity. Stale effects refuse every lifecycle, capacity, delivery and cleanup action. One shared_codex_error_is_retryable predicate drives both identity capture and the handler, so no Failed effect is dropped silently.
